note.title: Identity and relationships with others
note.specFocus: family, friendship, personality and healthy relationships
note.sourcePages: Original practice material written around common GCSE-style language themes; not official exam-board material.
note.summary:
1.1 Identity and relationships with others
Key focus
- family, friendship, personality and healthy relationships.

Core language
- Useful structures: मेरे विचार में; मुझे ... पसंद है क्योंकि; पिछले साल; अगली बार; आम तौर पर; मुझे ... चाहिए।
- Nouns and adjectives agree in gender and number; use present, past and future time markers consistently.

Exam tips
- For comprehension, locate the exact word or phrase that proves each answer.
- In translation, preserve tense, negatives, quantities and relationships between people.
- In writing, add opinions and reasons, vary time frames, and check verb and adjective agreement.

questions.examTip: Read the Hindi carefully and answer with the stated detail; check नहीं, समय words, numbers and the subject of the verb.
questions.modelAnswer: There are four people in my family: my parents, my younger sister and me.
questions.question:
Reading comprehension. Read the Hindi sentence and answer in English:

“मेरे परिवार में चार लोग हैं: माता-पिता, मेरी छोटी बहन और मैं।”

How many people are in the family, and who are they?

questions.examTip: Read the Hindi carefully and answer with the stated detail; check नहीं, समय words, numbers and the subject of the verb.
questions.modelAnswer: My mother always listens to me, so we get on very well.
questions.question:

“मेरी माँ हमेशा मेरी बात सुनती हैं, इसलिए हमारी बहुत अच्छी बनती है।”

Why does the speaker get on well with her mother?

questions.modelAnswer: In my opinion, honesty is the most important quality in a friend.

Which quality does the speaker value most in a friend?
